---
title: "Spatial domain: ICCAT grid, stock areas and regions"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8,
                      fig.height = 5, dev = "ragg_png", dpi = 110)
```

Every simulation runs on a **spatial domain**: a set of cells on a regular
1x1 degree lattice, each with an identifier, a representative point, a
geodesic area and a latitudinal region. A domain is an object of class
`om_domain` with the same components as the domain of Experimento 02:

| component | content |
|---|---|
| `cells` | one row per cell: `Cell_ID`, `Longitude`, `Latitude`, `Nominal_lon0`, `Nominal_lat0` (south-west corner of the nominal cell), `Row`, `Col` (lattice indices), `Area_km2`, `Area_frac` (fraction of the nominal cell that is sea), `Region` |
| `geometry` | `sf` polygons of the cells (used only by maps) |
| `lattice` | origin and size of the integer lattice used by the Gaussian random fields |
| `regions` | latitude `breaks` and `labels` of the regions |
| `meta` | provenance (source, stock code, area method, bounding box, ...) |

```{r setup}
library(pelagicOM)
library(ggplot2)
```

## The bundled ICCAT 1x1 grid

The package ships the 10,051 cells of the official ICCAT 1x1 grid
(layer `grids_01x01` of the ICCAT GIS GeoPackage). The cells are clipped by
the coastline and their areas are geodesic. `om_domain_iccat()` builds a
domain from it without any GIS file. For the BET-A stock area the result is
exactly the domain of Experimento 02:

```{r}
dom <- om_domain_iccat("BET-A")
dom
head(dom$cells)
str(dom$lattice)
```

Coastal cells are only partly sea (`Area_frac < 1`) and high-latitude cells
are smaller. The geodesic area is therefore what turns density (t/km²) into
biomass (t):

```{r, fig.height = 4}
ggplot(dom$cells, aes(Latitude, Area_km2, colour = Area_frac < 1)) +
    geom_point(size = 0.4) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("black", "grey65"),
                        labels = c("open ocean", "coastal (clipped)")) +
    labs(y = "Cell area (km²)", colour = NULL) +
    theme_pub()
```

## ICCAT stock areas

Every stock area of the ICCAT GeoPackage is available. A cell belongs to a
stock area when a point on its surface lies inside the stock polygon. BET-A
is identical to the ICCAT Convention area, so it keeps all cells, as in
Experimento 02.

```{r}
knitr::kable(iccat_stocks()[, c("stock_code", "name", "n_cells")])
```

```{r, fig.height = 6}
show_stocks <- function(codes) {
    g <- iccat_geometry()
    do.call(rbind, lapply(codes, function(cd) {
        d <- om_domain_iccat(cd, geometry = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
        x <- g[g$Cell_ID %in% d$cells$Cell_ID, ]
        x$stock <- cd
        x
    }))
}
m <- show_stocks(c("ALB-N", "ALB-S", "ALB-M", "SKJ-E", "SKJ-W", "BFT-W"))
ggplot(m) +
    geom_sf(fill = "grey30", colour = NA) +
    facet_wrap(~stock, ncol = 3) +
    coord_sf(expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = "Cells of some ICCAT stock areas") +
    theme_pub(base = 9) +
    theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank())
```

## Latitudinal regions

Regions are latitude bands defined by ascending `region_breaks` and by
`region_labels` listed **from north to south**. The default is the rule of
Experimento 02: R01 for lat > 20, R02 for -20 ≤ lat ≤ 20 and R03 for
lat < -20.

```{r}
classify_regions(c(-35, -20, 0, 20, 35))
table(dom$cells$Region)
```

Any number of bands can be used. Regions without cells in a domain are
dropped with a message:

```{r, fig.height = 4.5}
dom_alb <- om_domain_iccat("ALB-N", region_breaks = c(25, 40),
                           region_labels = c("NORTH", "CENTRAL", "SOUTH"))
table(dom_alb$cells$Region)
g <- dom_alb$geometry
g$Region <- dom_alb$cells$Region
ggplot(g) +
    geom_sf(aes(fill = Region), colour = NA) +
    scale_fill_grey(start = 0.25, end = 0.8) +
    coord_sf(expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = "ALB-N with three regions") +
    theme_pub() + theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank())
```

The regions are part of the domain. They are copied into the configuration
of the simulation, and they decide which cells each fleet can fish and how
the scenario data sets are filtered.

## Reading a GeoPackage

`om_domain_from_gpkg()` is the function that built the domain of
Experimento 02 from `ICCAT_gis.gpkg`. It works as follows:

1. It reads the grid layer and a stock-area layer.
2. It repairs invalid geometries.
3. It keeps the cells that belong to the stock.
4. It computes geodesic areas with `lwgeom`.
5. It derives the lattice indices and the regions.

With the defaults it returns the cells, lattice and polygons of Experimento 02
exactly (this is checked by the package tests).

```{r, eval = FALSE}
gpkg <- "Experimento_02/ICCAT/ICCAT_gis.gpkg"
inspect_geopackage(gpkg, layers = "albacore_tuna_stock_areas")

dom_bet <- om_domain_from_gpkg(gpkg)                      # BET-A, Exp. 02
dom_alb <- om_domain_from_gpkg(gpkg,
                               layer_stock = "albacore_tuna_stock_areas",
                               stock_code = "ALB-S",
                               selection = "point_on_surface")
```

The `selection` argument chooses the rule:

* `"intersects"` keeps every cell that touches the stock polygon. This is
  the rule of Experimento 02 and is adequate when the stock area is the whole
  Convention area.
* `"point_on_surface"` keeps a cell when a point on its surface lies inside
  the polygon. Cells that only share an edge with the boundary of a smaller
  stock area are left out, and the cells are the same as those of
  `om_domain_iccat()`.

A simulation can also read the GeoPackage itself, through
`spatial$source = "gpkg"` in the biomass configuration:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
cfg <- om_biomass_config("BET_ICCAT",
                         spatial = list(source = "gpkg", gpkg = gpkg))
sim <- simulate_biomass(cfg)    # identical to the bundled-grid run
```

## Synthetic grids

For teaching, tests or other oceans, `om_domain_grid()` builds a
rectangular 1x1 grid. `exclude` removes cells (for example land) through a
function of the cell centres. Areas are geodesic on the WGS84 ellipsoid,
computed exactly as for the ICCAT grid.

```{r, fig.height = 4}
basin <- om_domain_grid(lon = c(40, 100), lat = c(-40, 20),
                        exclude = function(lon, lat) lat > 10 & lon < 60,
                        region_breaks = c(-15),
                        region_labels = c("NORTH", "SOUTH"))
basin
g <- basin$geometry; g$Region <- basin$cells$Region
ggplot(g) + geom_sf(aes(fill = Region), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.05) +
    scale_fill_grey(start = 0.3, end = 0.7) + theme_pub()
```

`geodesic_area_km2()` gives the area of any polygon in geographic
coordinates:

```{r}
cell <- sf::st_sfc(sf::st_polygon(list(cbind(c(0, 1, 1, 0, 0),
                                             c(0, 0, 1, 1, 0)))), crs = 4326)
geodesic_area_km2(cell)
```

## Using a domain

By default `simulate_biomass()` builds the domain described in
`cfg$spatial` (the bundled grid and the BET-A area for the `BET_ICCAT`
preset). Any other domain can be passed explicitly. Its regions then take
precedence over the ones in the configuration:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
sim <- simulate_biomass(om_biomass_config("BET_ICCAT"), domain = dom_alb)
```

See [Tuning the operating model](tuning.html) for complete examples with other stock areas.
